source_refs.note: Book p. 106: 6.8 A.G.P. definition (corresponding terms of an A.P. and a G.P. multiplied), general A.G.P. ab, (a+d)br, ... and its nth term {a+(n-1)d}br^(n-1)

blocks.text: Ab tak humne do qisam ki progressions parhi: A.P., jis mein har term pichli mein ek fixed number \(d\) jama karne se banti hai, aur G.P., jis mein har term pichli ko ek fixed number \(r\) se zarb dene se banti hai. Aaj hum in dono ko mila kar ek nayi qisam banayenge: arithmetico-geometric progression (A.G.P.). Naam hi bata raha hai: 'arithmetico' (A.P. wala hissa) aur 'geometric' (G.P. wala hissa).

Kitab kehti hai: maan lijiye \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n, \ldots\) ek A.P. hai aur \(b_1, b_2, b_3, \ldots, b_n, \ldots\) ek G.P. hai. To A.P. aur G.P. ki corresponding (ek hi position wali) terms ko zarb dene se jo sequence banti hai, yani \(a_1b_1, a_2b_2, a_3b_3, \ldots, a_nb_n, \ldots\), use arithmetico-geometric sequence kehte hain.
Ab ek general A.P. lijiye: \(a, a + d, a + 2d, \ldots, \{a + (n - 1)d\}\), aur ek general G.P.: \(b, br, br^{2}, \ldots, br^{n-1}\), jahan \(r \ne 1\).

A.P. aur G.P. ki corresponding terms ko zarb dene se yeh arithmetico-geometric sequence milti hai:
\[ab,\ (a + d)br,\ (a + 2d)br^{2},\]
\[\ldots,\ \{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\]

Is liye A.G.P. ki \(n\)th term, A.P. ki \(n\)th term aur G.P. ki \(n\)th term ka product (hasil-e-zarb) hai. Yani aisi sequence ki \(n\)th term ki shakal yeh hai:
\[\{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\]

blocks.title: Kyun
blocks.text: \(n\)th term yeh kyun hai? A.P. ki \(n\)th term ka formula aap jaante hain: \(a + (n - 1)d\). G.P. ki \(n\)th term: \(br^{n-1}\). A.G.P. ki term inhi dono ka zarb hai, to \(n\)th term bhi dono \(n\)th terms ka zarb: \(\{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\). Koi naya formula yaad nahin karna, sirf purane do formulas jor dene hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
'Corresponding' ka matlab hai same position: pehli ko pehli se, doosri ko doosri se zarb. Har A.G.P. term ke do hisse hain: ek 'coefficient' wala hissa (\(a, a + d, a + 2d, \ldots\)) jo har baar \(d\) jama hone se barhta hai, aur ek 'power' wala hissa (\(b, br, br^{2}, \ldots\)) jo har baar \(r\) se zarb hota hai.
\(r \ne 1\) kyun? Agar \(r = 1\) ho to G.P. sirf \(b, b, b, \ldots\) hai, aur zarb dene se seedhi saadi A.P. hi banti hai (har term \(b\) guna). Koi nayi cheez nahin, is liye is case ko alag rakha gaya.
Ek chhoti si misaal se dekhte hain ke A.G.P. kaise banti hai. A.P. \(1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots\) aur G.P. \(1, 2, 4, 8, \ldots\) lijiye aur term ba term zarb dijiye:

blocks.caption: A.G.P. ko term ba term banana (hamari misaal)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table se teen baatein seekhiye:
1. A.G.P. \(1, 4, 12, 32, \ldots\) na A.P. hai (farq \(3, 8, 20\) barabar nahin) na G.P. (ratio \(4, 3, \frac{8}{3}\) barabar nahin). Yeh dono ka mixture hai.
2. \(n\)th term \(n \cdot 2^{n-1}\) hai: A.P. ki \(n\)th term \(n\), G.P. ki \(2^{n-1}\).
3. Dono hisse hamesha same \(n\) par chalte hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
A.G.P. ko pehchaanne ka tareeqa: har term ko do factors mein toriye. \(1\cdot 2 + 3\cdot 4 + 5\cdot 8 + \cdots\) mein pehle factors \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\) A.P. mein hain (\(a = 1\), \(d = 2\)), aur doosre factors \(2, 4, 8, \ldots\) G.P. mein (\(b = 2\), \(r = 2\)).
\(n\)th term: \(\{1 + (n - 1)2\}\cdot 2\cdot 2^{n-1} = (2n - 1)2^{n}\).
Tasdeeq: \(n = 3\) par \((5)(8) = 40\), aur series ki teesri term \(5\cdot 8 = 40\) hai. Sahi!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. A.P. \(2, 5, 8, \ldots\) aur G.P. \(1, 3, 9, \ldots\) se bani A.G.P. ki pehli teen terms kya hongi?
2. Us A.G.P. ki \(n\)th term ka formula likhiye.
3. Kya \(3, 6, 12, 24\) A.G.P. hai, ya sirf G.P.?

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. A.G.P. = A.P. aur G.P. ki corresponding terms ka zarb.
2. \(ab, (a + d)br, (a + 2d)br^{2}, \ldots\)
3. \(n\)th term: \(\{a + (n - 1)d\}br^{n-1}\).
4. Dono factors mein position same: \(a_nb_n\).
5. \(r \ne 1\); warna yeh sirf A.P. reh jati hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. A.P. ki \(n\)th term ko G.P. ki \((n+1)\)th term se zarb dena, yani \(r^{n-1}\) ki jagah \(r^{n}\) likhna.
2. A.G.P. ko G.P. samajh kar common ratio dhoondna: \(1, 4, 12, 32\) mein koi ek ratio nahin.
3. A.P. term ko \(a + (n - 1)d\) ki jagah \(a + nd\) likh dena.
4. Factors torte waqt A.P. aur G.P. wale hisse ulat dena; G.P. wala hissa woh hai jo zarb se barhta hai.
